Question numbers run 1-39 unbroken. Instruction (viii) prints NO count of internal choices, so the roster was built by walking the marking scheme (ms pages 0-10, footer X_086_31/2/3 on every page, a per-set scheme): a bare OR in Q24, 25, 27, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38, 39 = 9 alternatives, each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper. No void note anywhere in the scheme (the Q38(c)(i) note 'award full marks even if only labelled ray diagram is given' is conditional marking latitude). All 20 Section-A answers are CBSE's own, read off the scheme page images; each re-derived, one disagreement (Q19, flagged). Decimal points on this paper are RAISED (Q2: 6{\cdot}1; Q31: 1{\cdot}5). Follower of 31/2/1: 41 of 54 rows copied byte-for-byte from 2025-31-2-1 after confirming each on this paper's page (the shared A-R instruction keeps the printed em dash, as the reference does, so it dedups); 13 rows transcribed fresh: Q1, Q6, Q9, Q13, Q17, Q19, Q22, Q23, Q26, Q28, Q30, Q31, Q33. Every _figure written from this paper's own pages.

options.label: B

questions._flag: Key disagreement. CBSE keys (C) 'A is true, but R is false.' Re-derived: A is true (bending the wire changes neither its length nor its area of cross-section), and R also reads as true, since R = rho l / A makes the resistance of a wire of given dimensions directly proportional to its resistivity; R does not explain A, which gives (B). CBSE's key kept; the scheme presumably reads R as false because resistance also depends on length and area. For a human.

(i) Define the term decomposition reaction. Write one chemical equation each for decomposition reaction where energy is supplied in the form of heat, light or electricity.

(ii) Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost is considered an exothermic reaction. Why ?

Why are decomposition reactions called the opposite of combination reactions ? Write one chemical equation each for these two types of reactions mentioning the name of the reactant(s) and the product(s) involved in the reactions.

Two substances ‘A’ and ‘B’ are burnt in air separately. For ‘A’, ashes are collected and dissolved in water to get solution ‘X’, while for ‘B’, fumes produced are passed through water to get solution ‘Y’. Both the solutions ‘X’ and ‘Y’ are then tested with pH paper.

(a) If ‘X’ gives light blue colour and ‘Y’ gives orange colour to the pH paper, then write the nature and range of pH of ‘X’ and ‘Y’.

(b) Which one of the two – A and B, is a metal ? Justify your answer.

(a) Define hormone.

(b) “Hormones should be secreted in precise quantities. We have a feedback mechanism through which this is done.” With the help of an example justify the statement.

(a) Work out the pattern of inheritance in this case.

(b) What will be the ratio of plants obtained in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation ?
